evidence_policy: Real organizations and public URLs, not customers, partners, verified demand, sent outreach or delivered projects.

prospects.mcp_status: A Judge.me Email MCP is documented; a first-party reviews API MCP was not confirmed in this research.
prospects.task: Let merchant agents retrieve source-backed rating summaries and published review evidence for one product.
prospects.offer: API Agent Launch; scoped reviews data access
prospects.hypothesis: A specific reviews intelligence workflow can complement its existing integrations without duplicating its Email MCP.
prospects.subject: Judge.me reviews API → verified product-review tools for AI merchants
prospects.pitch: Your Reviews API and technology partner pathway suggest a practical opportunity: a small, source-backed MCP toolset for merchants to ask for product rating summaries and supporting published reviews in one named AI client. We know Judge.me Email has an MCP connection; this proposal targets review retrieval, not the Email MCP. Could we agree on one approved merchant use case and API scope for a test?

prospects.mcp_status: Public REST API is documented; general first-party customer-data MCP was not verified here. Re-check before pitching.
prospects.task: Let authorized CX analysts retrieve survey status and response aggregates in an agent without exporting raw customer responses.
prospects.hypothesis: CX teams may value a narrow, approved summary layer over exposing entire survey APIs.
prospects.subject: SurveySparrow API: scoped AI assistant access to survey insights
prospects.pitch: Your REST API and partner ecosystem could support a narrow agent-facing use case: an authorized CX user asks for survey status and response summaries without manually exporting data. We would start with an approved read-only source, two agreed acceptance tests and one supported client. Is there a relevant integrations owner to evaluate this with?

prospects.mcp_status: Public store API and app-submission pathway documented; an official Ecwid store-data MCP was not verified here.
prospects.task: Merchant-authorized read-only lookup of catalog and inventory through a customer AI assistant.
prospects.offer: Agency/marketplace pilot, private auth scoped separately
prospects.hypothesis: A focused merchant use case and install guide could be submitted through the existing Ecwid app process.
prospects.subject: Ecwid merchant catalog: focused agent-readiness pilot
prospects.pitch: Ecwid already has a documented store API and app marketplace. We would like to validate a deliberately small merchant-owned AI workflow: product search and current availability, with permissions and tested connection steps. This is not a claim that Ecwid lacks its own AI roadmap; could you point us to the integration-review process for an approved pilot?

prospects.mcp_status: Public API confirmed. Third-party MCP integrations exist; first-party general fulfillment MCP not confirmed.
prospects.task: Allow print-on-demand sellers to check approved catalog variant availability and product metadata in an AI client.
prospects.offer: Scoped Launch or API partner integration
prospects.hypothesis: Catalog research is safer to pilot than fulfillment mutations or billable order placement.
prospects.subject: Printful API: read-only product research in customer AI assistants
prospects.pitch: We are exploring a read-only, merchant-authorized Printful API workflow for product and variant lookup directly from a named AI assistant. Unlike generic API conversion, we would define accepted tasks, source freshness, and install instructions. Would your developer or partner team consider reviewing a narrowly scoped external integration?

prospects.mcp_status: Community MCP proposals/third-party implementations exist; first-party supported core MCP not established from official sources reviewed.
prospects.task: Give publication editors read-only access to published article metadata and topic discovery through an assistant.
prospects.offer: Open-source adapter demo plus integration distribution
prospects.hypothesis: A content-read use case can validate demand before authenticated Admin API work.
prospects.subject: Ghost Content API: reproducible read-only agent workflow proposal
prospects.pitch: I saw the Ghost community discussions around native MCP. We can contribute a narrow, testable Content API use case for assistants—searching and retrieving published posts, with no admin tokens. If useful, we can post a reproducible demonstration and get community feedback before asking for any formal integration listing.

prospects.mcp_status: A Sentry-built community MCP is acknowledged in Plausible docs; a first-party supported MCP is an official roadmap request.
prospects.task: Query website trend summaries with explicit metric definitions, time windows and no raw personal event data.
prospects.offer: Agent tool-evaluation / reliable hosted integration collaboration
prospects.hypothesis: Reliability, metric correctness and documented host setup might complement existing community MCP.
prospects.subject: Plausible Stats API + agent answers: accuracy-focused integration test
prospects.pitch: Plausible already acknowledges the community-built MCP from Sentry and has a dedicated feature request. Rather than suggesting another generic wrapper, we can test a bounded Stats API workflow for accurate period comparisons, explicit metric definitions and reproducible failure handling. Would documented evaluation results help your MCP roadmap?

prospects.mcp_status: Teamleader Orbit has an announced MCP; do not infer that Focus has no AI or MCP capabilities. Focus offers its own API and marketplace.
prospects.task: Authorized small-business staff query sales pipeline and draft quotation status without modifying records.
prospects.hypothesis: A Focus-specific, tested task layer may be valuable despite existing Orbit MCP.
prospects.subject: Teamleader Focus API: targeted AI assistant integration for quote lookups
prospects.pitch: I saw Teamleader Orbit's MCP announcement and Focus's separate developer/Marketplace API. Rather than duplicate Orbit, we would like to discuss a narrowly scoped Focus customer task: read authorized opportunities and quotation status from a named AI client. Is a custom integration submission the right path for a proof-of-value?

prospects.mcp_status: AI features announced; current X-Series documentation did not establish a broadly supported official MCP interface. Verify with partner team.
prospects.task: Retailer inventory lookup by SKU and location using existing customer-granted API scope.
prospects.hypothesis: A merchant-operated agent query may complement native Lightspeed AI, not replace it.
prospects.subject: Lightspeed Retail API: merchant-directed SKU lookup from AI assistants
prospects.pitch: Lightspeed is already investing in native AI, so we are not pitching a generic MCP generator. We are proposing a small retailer-controlled inventory lookup use case for an external assistant, supported by documented API permissions and named-client tests. Would the developer-partner team review this integration category?

prospects.mcp_status: Recharge Analytics MCP Early Adopter Program exists; generic analytics MCP creation is not a viable differentiator.
prospects.task: Merchant support agent reads a subscription's state, billing interval and safe change policies before any modification.
prospects.offer: Technology partner pilot for non-analytics merchant support
prospects.hypothesis: Focus on merchant support permissions and source-scoped read workflows, not a second analytics MCP.
prospects.subject: Recharge API: non-analytics merchant-support MCP use case
prospects.pitch: Recharge already has an Analytics MCP early-adopter offering. Our proposal is different: a permissioned merchant-support read workflow for subscription status and plan policy, with no billing changes or customer action until separately authorized. Is this a relevant gap for your technology-partner team to explore?

prospects.mcp_status: Official Jobber MCP / ChatGPT and Claude connector already launched; do not sell a duplicate general MCP.
prospects.task: Evaluate a specific permitted field-service job-status use case and document AI client acceptance, rather than recreating Jobber MCP.
prospects.offer: Integration QA / vertical workflow, only after validated gap
prospects.hypothesis: Existing native MCP lowers fit; only pursue a verified integration/QA pain.
prospects.subject: Jobber MCP already exists — proposal to validate a specific customer workflow
prospects.pitch: We see that Jobber already ships an official MCP connector. We are not proposing another general connector. If there is a documented gap in a field-service workflow or in external client acceptance, Foundry can run targeted task tests and supply reusable technical evidence. Would your developer team consider a narrow gap assessment?
